pinterest.title: Oceania Wedding Destinations From Fiji to Tahiti
pinterest.description: Oceania wedding destinations run from Fiji, Vanuatu and New Caledonia to Tahiti, the Cook Islands, Samoa, Tonga and Hawaii, then on to New Zealand and the Whitsundays. Our guide groups ten unranked places by region, each with its weather months, its legal or symbolic route and the questions to ask a venue before guests book. A calm way to compare South Pacific wedding destinations side by side.

pinterest.title: Pacific Island Wedding Destinations for a Lagoon Ceremony
pinterest.description: Tahiti and French Polynesia pair lagoons and volcanic peaks with paperwork in French, arranged through the mairie of the commune. In the Cook Islands, the Ministry of Justice sets out a licence after you both give notice in person, and the ceremony takes place at the site the licence names. Smartraveller dates the cyclone season for both from November to April, so ask each venue where the ceremony moves if an alert is raised.

pinterest.title: Planning Oceania Wedding Destinations Around Cyclone Season
pinterest.description: Smartraveller dates the cyclone season from November to April for the South Pacific islands in our guide, and to May in New Caledonia. For a wedding in those months, write the weather into the contract: a covered space for the full guest list, who calls the move and by what hour, and the postponement terms if a cyclone suspends flights. Give guests a buffer day either side of the wedding. More planning notes in our Oceania guide.

slides: Ten Oceania wedding destinations, from Fiji to Tahiti, grouped by region and unranked
Melanesia. Fiji, Vanuatu and New Caledonia. Smartraveller dates a cyclone season opening in November for all three, so plan a covered space and a buffer day.
Polynesia. Tahiti and French Polynesia for lagoons and volcanic peaks, then the Cook Islands, Samoa and Tonga, with Hawaii far to the north.
In Samoa and Tonga, Sunday shapes the wedding weekend. Ask each venue about music, alcohol service and guest transfers before you set the date.
New Zealand swaps the reef for lakes, vineyards and mountains. Visitors can apply for the marriage licence online before they fly.
Closer to home, the Whitsundays offer island ceremonies and boat days under Australian law, with no passport needed.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Fiji or Tahiti? New Zealand or the Whitsundays? Oceania gives you reef islands, lagoons and lakes within reach of Australia, and what separates them for a wedding is the calendar, the paperwork and how easily your guests get there.

Our new guide, Oceania Wedding Destinations From Fiji to Tahiti, covers ten unranked places grouped by region.

Melanesia
Fiji, Vanuatu and New Caledonia sit close to home. Smartraveller dates a cyclone season opening in November for all three, so a covered ceremony space and a buffer day belong in the plan. Check Smartraveller's latest advice for New Caledonia before you book.

Polynesia
Tahiti and French Polynesia for lagoons and volcanic peaks, with paperwork in French through the mairie of the commune. The Cook Islands, where the Ministry of Justice sets out a licence step by step. Samoa and Tonga, where Sunday shapes the weekend. And Hawaii, far to the north, with a cloudier, stormier winter from October to April.

New Zealand and the Whitsundays
Lakes, vineyards and mountains, with a licence you can apply for online before you fly. Or island ceremonies and boat days under Australian law, with no passport needed.

Questions worth asking any venue
Which covered space seats every guest, and who calls the move?
What happens to our deposits if a cyclone moves the date?
How do guests reach the property if roads, flights or boats are held up?

Legal or symbolic, the route differs by country. This is general information, not legal advice, so check with each destination's authorities.

Down to two islands? Message us to weigh them against your guest list with a Wedded Advisor. Full guide at the link in bio.
